title: Quantum Sphaera Companion: A Structure-First Mathematical Unfolding — full Companion and physics paper
description:
Quantum Sphaera Companion v5.5.0 is a minor version of the database-backed v5 release. As before, it comprises two complementary English documents from one source snapshot: the full Companion with its research history, and the physics paper Graded carriers and physical readouts: conditions for mass and geometric interpretation.

New in the full Companion are the research layers v4.10.0-r60 to r68. They record: a family SO(3) on the Albert algebra as the commutant of G2 in F4, its breaking to exactly A4 by the charge as a single spin-3 tensor, a no-go for quark mixing under exact A4, and a vacuum alignment that depends on free coefficients (r60); corrections of two formula slips in earlier layers, which change no number, test result or status (r61); octonion copies in the sedenions and on the next Cayley-Dickson levels: three copies per doubling, which are not three generations, a remainder generation whose physical status is not shown, no masses from the copy structure alone, and a real line that is a neutral scalar and not a spin-2 graviton (r62); the Koide point as the fixed point of an exchange of matter-type and tachyon-type states, which holds the Koide value only with a set scale and with a postulate of equal standing of the two frames that the author adopted as a working assumption, while the phase 2/9 remains a fit (r63); a record of further tests, among them a recursive field equation on the tower that fixes no scale, mixing built from the copies, a rule to transfer a prediction to the matter frame before comparing it with data, and an open prediction of area steps and gravitational-wave echoes with a deadline in 2028, together with precisions to earlier layers from an audit of the stand-alone physics article (r64); charge axis and charge type on the sedenion carrier, where the relative orientation of leptons and quarks holds for every axis and both charge types but depends on one named setting (r65); the number beta_sym as the overlap of the Hopf state with the antipode of the photon pole under one named reading, an identity for every value that does not derive the number (r66); and the counting rule adopted by the author on 26 November 2026 as a postulate, from which beta_sym = 0.5494056410 and gamma_L = 1.8646997646 are computed and become the reference values (r67); and a recalculation of all numbers that depend on beta_sym at the reference value, an exploration that changes no recorded verdict (r68).

New in the physics paper: a development section in the masses part on the family symmetry, the octonion copies and the Koide point on the tower (r60 to r65), including the restriction of the statement on the relative CP sign; additions to the section on the one number and its several translations on the recursive field equation (r64), the two-readout reading (r66) and the counting postulate with its reference value and the refuted closure test (r67); and one sentence on a recalculation of the dependent numbers at the reference value, an exploration that changes no verdict (r68). The research catalogue gains eleven entries.

Scope: this is a conditional mathematical-physics research programme, not a completed unified theory. No native lepton spectrum, absolute physical mass scale, general gravitational field equations or closure of the open problems is established by this release. The counting rule is a postulate, not derived; so is the equal standing of the matter and the tachyon frame. A postulate closes no open problem: OP1 to OP5, C5 and C6/T2 remain open, and OP1 now reads "derive the counting postulate". Most results of r60 to r68 are explorations or tests marked as not blind in whole or in part. Refuted were, among others: the pre-registered counts of octonion copies on the higher levels and the prediction that no remainder generation exists (r62); the pre-registered dimension of the derivation algebra over the sedenions, CP violation in the mixing built from the copies, and three tests of the recursive field equation (r64); and the test whether a closure condition fixes beta_sym without the counting rule (H165, r67). The number of generations, the charge axis, the Brannen phase, the Koide overlap, the orientation of the octant step and the identification of sources in the OP5 case remain inputs or open. Database registration, hashes and provenance checks do not constitute proof of physical interpretation. The manuscript has undergone documented self-review, not independent peer review.

The package contains two English PDFs, compilable sources, a database snapshot and checksum manifests. Both document editions retain open argument-review obligations.

Version DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24563811. Concept DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.19210728.
